message.content:
### Building a New PC – Step‑by‑Step Guide

Below is a practical, beginner‑friendly walkthrough.  
Feel free to skip sections you already know, but keep the order for safety and best results.

| # | What to Do | Why It Matters | Tips |
|---|------------|----------------|------|
| 1 | **Plan & Budget** | Know what you’ll use it for (gaming, video editing, office, etc.) | List required specs: CPU, GPU, RAM, storage, PSU, case, cooling. |
| 2 | **Gather Parts** | All components must be compatible. | Use a PC build calculator (e.g., PCPartPicker) to avoid conflicts. |
| 3 | **Prepare Workspace** | Clean, static‑free area. | Anti‑static wrist strap or work on a non‑conductive mat. |
| 4 | **Open the Case** | Access to motherboard, power supply, drives. | Remove side panels; keep screws handy. |
| 5 | **Install the Power Supply (PSU)** | Supplies power to all components. | Align the PSU with the rear fan mount, screw it in, route cables. |
| 6 | **Mount the Motherboard** | Base for all other components. | Align standoffs, screw in, connect 24‑pin ATX + 8‑pin EPS. |
| 7 | **Install the CPU** | Central processing unit. | Open the socket latch, align the CPU (triangle marker), gently place, lock. |
| 8 | **Apply Thermal Paste & Install CPU Cooler** | Keeps CPU from overheating. | Use a pea‑size amount; install cooler per its instructions. |
| 9 | **Insert RAM** | Memory for multitasking. | Open DIMM slots, align notch, press until clicks. |
| 10 | **Mount Storage (SSD/HDD)** | Data storage. | For M.2 SSDs, slide into the M.2 slot; for SATA drives, use drive bays or brackets. |
| 11 | **Install the Graphics Card (GPU)** | Handles rendering for games, video, etc. | Insert into the top PCI‑e x16 slot, secure with screws, connect 6/8‑pin power. |
| 12 | **Connect All Cables** | Power, data, front panel, USB, audio. | Refer to motherboard manual for exact pinouts. |
| 13 | **Cable Management** | Improves airflow & aesthetics. | Tuck cables behind the motherboard tray, use zip ties. |
| 14 | **Close the Case** | Protect components, finish look. | Reattach side panels, double‑check all screws. |
| 15 | **First Boot & BIOS Setup** | Verify hardware, set boot order. | Press the power button; if nothing happens, double‑check connections. |
| 16 | **Install Operating System (OS)** | Turn your PC into a usable machine. | Use a USB flash drive with Windows 10/11 or Linux; follow on‑screen prompts. |
| 17 | **Install Drivers & Updates** | Ensure hardware works optimally. | Download latest drivers from manufacturer sites. |
| 18 | **Test & Benchmark** | Confirm stability, performance. | Run stress tests (Prime95, FurMark) and benchmarks (Cinebench, 3DMark). |
| 19 | **Enjoy & Maintain** | Keep your system running smoothly. | Clean dust every 3–6 months, update firmware, monitor temperatures. |

---

#### Quick Checklist

- **CPU** – Intel i5/i7/i9 or AMD Ryzen 5/7/9
- **Motherboard** – Matching socket, chipset, form factor (ATX, mATX, mini‑ITX)
- **RAM** – 16 GB DDR4/DDR5 (minimum 8 GB for basic use)
- **GPU** – NVIDIA RTX 3060/3070/3080 or AMD Radeon RX 6600/6700/6800
- **Storage** – NVMe SSD (250 GB–1 TB) + optional SATA HDD
- **PSU** – 550 W–750 W, 80+ Gold or better
- **Case** – ATX mid‑tower or mini‑ITX, good airflow
- **Cooling** – Stock cooler or aftermarket air/liquid cooler
- **Operating System** – Windows 10/11 or Linux distro

---

#### Common Pitfalls & How to Avoid Them

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| **Short‑circuit** | Use anti‑static wrist strap; never touch metal contacts while components are powered. |
| **CPU not seated** | Double‑check the socket latch; ensure the CPU is aligned correctly. |
| **GPU not recognized** | Verify power connectors are fully seated; check BIOS for PCI‑e settings. |
| **No POST** | Check all power connectors, remove any loose cables, ensure the motherboard is on standoffs. |
| **Overheating** | Ensure proper airflow, clean dust, apply adequate thermal paste. |

---

#### Resources

- **PCPartPicker** – Build planner & compatibility checker.  
- **YouTube Channels** – *Linus Tech Tips*, *JayzTwoCents*, *Paul’s Hardware* for visual guides.  
- **Manufacturer Manuals** – Always read the motherboard, PSU, and GPU manuals for specific instructions.  

Happy building! If you hit a snag, let me know which step and I’ll help troubleshoot.
